title: Frostbite
summary: Prevent refreezing, rewarm in controlled 37–40°C water when safe, and obtain prompt medical care.
sources: 2024 American Heart Association and American Red Cross Guidelines for First Aid — Frostbite
actions: Move out of wind and cold, remove wet clothing and constricting items, and check first for hypothermia.
Do not thaw tissue if it may refreeze. Protect it and arrange urgent transport.
When refreezing is not possible, immerse the area in clean lukewarm water at 37 to 40°C (99 to 104°F).
If water immersion is not possible, allow gradual warming in warm room air or against the person’s warm skin.
After thawing, place clean dry gauze loosely between digits and apply a bulky loose dressing. Avoid walking on thawed feet and seek prompt medical care.
prohibitions: Do not rub, massage, or apply snow.
Do not use fire, a heater, hair dryer, heating pad, or hot water.

emergencyCall.text: Confusion, drowsiness, stopped shivering, or abnormal breathing suggests dangerous hypothermia and requires emergency services.
